commands.author: Fatmylin

target.title: feat(line): per-user in-flight guard for concurrent message errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When LINE users send rapid consecutive messages, the earlier revision of this PR busy-skipped the second message at the webhook handler. Review feedback (correctly) pointed out that this bypasses core's active-run admission policy — sessions default to `steer`, so a rapid correction is supposed to be folded into the running turn, not dropped. Separately, when core steers a message and produces no standalone reply for it, LINE has no reactions, so the sender gets no visible signal that their follow-up was accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reworked to the shape requested in review:

- **No blocking, no busy replies.** Rapid same-user events always reach `processMessage`, and core queue policy (steer/followup/collect/interrupt) decides the outcome. The busy-reply path is removed entirely — LINE has no local queue that can fill, so there is no genuine cannot-admit case left.
- **Non-blocking in-flight tracker.** The per-user guard became a ref-counted tracker (`extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.ts`) whose only job is to flag events admitted while the sender's earlier event is still processing (`inFlightAtAdmission`, threaded through the inbound context). Senderless group/room events stay untracked (`@line/bot-sdk` marks source `userId` optional) so distinct users can never collapse onto one key.
- **Steering ack on silent turns.** Delivery (`extensions/line/src/monitor.ts`) sends a short reply-token acknowledgement only when a flagged turn ends with no standalone final reply (`hasFinalInboundReplyDispatch` false). In the common steer case the merged reply is delivered against the newest turn and is itself the visible feedback, so no ack fires; the ack covers the residual case where the turn ends silently. Best-effort reply-token only — never push.

## User Impact

- Rapid same-user follow-ups now steer into the running turn (or queue as followups, per core policy): a correction sent while the bot is composing gets incorporated into the final answer instead of being skipped
- No message is ever dropped or answered with a busy notice at the LINE layer
- If core absorbs a follow-up silently, the sender gets a lightweight "👀 Got it — I'm folding this into the reply I'm working on." acknowledgement instead of silence
- Different users in the same group are tracked independently; senderless events bypass tracking entirely

## Evidence

**Unit tests** (`pnpm test extensions/line` — bot-handlers suite 37/37):
- two rapid same-user messages both reach `processMessage`; the second is not busy-skipped and is flagged for steering ack ("admits rapid same-user messages and flags the second for steering ack")
- in-flight state clears after completion and after `processMessage` throws
- per-user isolation in groups (other user unflagged, same-user follow-up flagged)
- senderless group messages/postbacks admitted and never flagged
- rapid same-user media messages are admitted and downloaded (no skip path left)
- replay dedupe tests unchanged and green (dedupe still only dedupes actual redeliveries)

**Live LINE proof** (real Messaging API bot, gateway run from this branch; screenshots in the comment below):
- 1:1: long request ("寫一篇 500 字…文章") followed ~2s later by a correction ("等等改成三百字") — no busy skip; the run issued a second model call after the steer and produced one merged reply that explicitly addresses the correction ("不論字數長短…"). Session transcript and redacted gateway logs match.
- Group: two users' rapid mentions are both admitted and processed while the first run is active (`message received`/`message processed` for both, no skips, no busy replies).

**Scope note**: while validating the group path we found a pre-existing core delivery gap — when a second user's message steers into an active group run, the reply generated for the earlier turn is dropped at delivery (`visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads`), on `main` as well as this branch (which does not touch delivery/attribution paths). Filed separately with transcript + log evidence: see the linked issue in the review thread.

This PR supersedes openclaw/openclaw#96379 (earlier busy-guard approach; closed).
